title: ClashBot from Zero: Python, Tools and Machine Learning through this project
pace: About 3-6 hours per lesson. At ~10 h/week the course takes about 6-7 months; at ~15 h/week about 4-5 months. Projects take 1-2 weeks each.

parts.title: Part A - Your computer and the project's tools

lessons.title: Files, folders and paths: a tour of the ClashBot repo
lessons.summary: What a file and a folder are, absolute vs relative paths, Windows vs Linux paths, text vs binary files, and a guided walk through the repo's layout.

lessons.title: The terminal: Git Bash and PowerShell basics
lessons.summary: Commands, arguments and flags; cd, ls, cat, head, tail, grep, wc; pipes; reading the live supervisor log and the work ledger from the terminal.

lessons.title: Text formats the project lives on: Markdown, JSON, JSONL, YAML, CSV
lessons.summary: How HANDOFF.md, match logs (one JSON object per line), training configs and tables are written, and how to read each by eye.

lessons.title: Git: history, commits, diffs and why we commit carefully
lessons.summary: Repositories, commits, git log, git diff, git show, branches, push; reading this repo's history; why the project commits only its own paths and never pathspec-commits HANDOFF.md.

lessons.title: PROJECT 1: Explore the repo like an engineer
lessons.summary: Use only the terminal and git to answer real questions: when was CLXIII made live, how many commits touched the opponent learner, what the last 10 ledger lines say.

lessons.title: Running Python: scripts, the interpreter, virtual environments
lessons.summary: What Python is, running a .py file, why the project never pipes code into python on stdin, what a venv is and why icebow/.venv exists.

lessons.title: Values, variables and types: elixir and tower HP
lessons.summary: Integers, floats, strings, booleans, arithmetic, f-strings, rounding; modelling elixir (0-10, +1 every 2.8 s at 1x) and tower hit points.

lessons.title: Collections: a deck as a list, card stats as a dictionary
lessons.summary: Lists, tuples, dictionaries, sets; indexing and slicing; the Icebow deck as a list; looking up card costs in a dict.

lessons.title: Decisions and loops: simulating elixir over a match
lessons.summary: if / elif / else, comparison and boolean operators, for and while loops, range; a tick-by-tick elixir simulation with 2x and 3x elixir phases.

lessons.title: Functions: small reusable pieces
lessons.summary: def, parameters, return values, default arguments, docstrings, scope; writing can_afford(card, elixir) and the 4-card hand cycle.

lessons.title: Reading real data: files and JSON lines
lessons.summary: open, with, reading lines, json.loads, writing files; counting wins and losses in the project's own live match log.

lessons.title: Errors, tracebacks and debugging
lessons.summary: Reading a traceback top to bottom, common errors (KeyError, TypeError, ModuleNotFoundError like the 'no module named jpype' crash), try / except, print debugging, assert.

lessons.title: Modules, imports and packages
lessons.summary: import, from ... import, your own modules, packages and __init__.py, sys.path and PYTHONPATH (why the pod launch sets PYTHONPATH).

lessons.title: Classes and objects: Card, Unit and Tower
lessons.summary: class, __init__, methods, attributes, dataclasses; modelling a unit with HP that takes damage and a tower that targets it.

lessons.title: Pythonic tools: comprehensions, sorting, lambda, generators
lessons.summary: List and dict comprehensions, sorted with key=, lambda, enumerate, zip, any / all, generators; ranking opponent decks by how often we lose to them.

lessons.title: The standard library you will meet everywhere
lessons.summary: pathlib, argparse (command-line flags like --no-fast-plays), datetime and time zones, collections.Counter, hashlib (the project's sha checks), subprocess, logging.

lessons.title: Testing your code
lessons.summary: Why tests, assert-based checks, pytest basics, reading one of the project's tests, the idea of 'planted checks' and 'absent key = identical'.

lessons.title: Reading other people's code
lessons.summary: A method for reading an unfamiliar file: entry point, inputs, outputs, data flow; annotate the battle-log poller and the live stuck-watcher.

lessons.title: PROJECT 2: Your own live-match report script
lessons.summary: Build a command-line script with argparse that reads the live match log and prints win rate overall, by day and by opponent card, with tests.

parts.title: Part C - Data, probability and statistics

lessons.title: NumPy: arrays, shapes and vectorised maths
lessons.summary: ndarray, shape, dtype, indexing, broadcasting, sum / mean along axes; the arena as an 18 x 32 tile grid.

lessons.title: pandas: tables of matches
lessons.summary: DataFrame, reading JSON lines, filtering, groupby, merge, time series; win rate per day of the live account.

lessons.title: Plotting results with matplotlib
lessons.summary: Line, bar and histogram plots, labels, saving figures; a rolling win-rate chart.

lessons.title: Probability for games
lessons.summary: Random variables, Bernoulli and binomial (wins out of N matches), expected value, simulation with random and NumPy, seeds and reproducibility.

lessons.title: Uncertainty: standard error and confidence intervals
lessons.summary: Why 398/480 is not exactly 82.9%, standard error, Wilson and Clopper-Pearson intervals, 'CI low > 32.7%', how many matches you need to tell two bots apart.

lessons.title: Comparing things fairly: tests, paired designs, effect sizes
lessons.summary: Hypothesis tests, p-values and their traps, paired comparisons and common random numbers, standardised differences (the RMS d of human-likeness), the KS test, AUC.

lessons.title: Experiment design: one change, fresh data, pre-registration
lessons.summary: Controls, one change per experiment, dev vs fresh sets (FRESH1-8), why thresholds were frozen before scoring, overfitting to your own test set.

lessons.title: PROJECT 3: Is the bot getting better? A statistical report
lessons.summary: With pandas + matplotlib, compare two periods of live play: win rates with confidence intervals, a plot, and a written conclusion graded measured / plausible / contradicted.

parts.title: Part D - Clash Royale as a system: simulators and the live bot

lessons.title: The game as a machine: ticks, elixir, lanes, coordinates
lessons.summary: Ticks and match phases, the arena coordinate system (board forward = decreasing y), towers and lanes, the Icebow deck and its plan.

lessons.title: What a simulator is: state, step, determinism and RNG
lessons.summary: State + action -> next state, deterministic vs random, seeds, why exact replays matter; write a tiny one-lane battle simulator.

lessons.title: The project's engines: RoyaleSim, crforge (Java) and RoyaleGym (Rust)
lessons.summary: Data tables (csv_logic, card stats) vs behaviour code, table versions (16.402.22 vs 16.635.3), why the project moved to crforge.

lessons.title: Replay exactness: live logs -> extractor -> engine -> compare
lessons.summary: How a live match is rebuilt and replayed, 'exact apart from torn', the D1 / D2 goals, why most failures were observation gaps and not engine rules.

lessons.title: The live system: reader, decide, tap, supervisor
lessons.summary: Screen reading through adb, the decision loop, latency, the supervisor and navigator, the battle-log API poller, safe start / stop.

lessons.title: PROJECT 4: Build a mini Clash simulator
lessons.summary: A tick-based Python simulator: elixir, a 4-card cycle, units walking a lane, towers shooting, a deterministic seed, and tests that a replay with the same seed is identical.

parts.title: Part E - The other languages and remote computers

lessons.title: Bash scripting
lessons.summary: Variables, quoting, $1 arguments, if, for, functions, exit codes, pipes, background jobs; read the scripts that launch and evaluate the opponent arms.

lessons.title: PowerShell essentials for Windows
lessons.summary: Cmdlets, objects in pipes, Get-Process / Stop-Process, why the project stops processes by exact PID only.

lessons.title: Java basics: reading the crforge facade
lessons.summary: Static types, classes, methods, compiling with javac, the JVM and jar files; how Python talks to Java through JPype.

lessons.title: A glance at Rust
lessons.summary: Why a friend wrote RoyaleGym in Rust (speed, safety), reading a struct and a function signature; no Rust coding required.

lessons.title: Remote machines: SSH, pods, GPUs and resource limits
lessons.summary: SSH and keys, RunPod pods, CPU vs GPU, container limits (54 CPUs / 62 GB even when the host shows 256), disks that vanish on stop, nohup and setsid, tar pipes.

lessons.title: PROJECT 5: Automate a small experiment end to end
lessons.summary: A Bash + Python pipeline on the laptop: run your mini simulator with 20 seeds in parallel, collect results to JSON lines, summarise with a confidence interval, all started by one script.

lessons.title: What learning means: data, model, loss, training
lessons.summary: Supervised vs reinforcement learning, inputs and labels, a loss as 'how wrong', training as 'reduce the loss', generalisation.

lessons.title: Linear algebra you actually need
lessons.summary: Vectors, dot products, matrices, matrix-vector products in NumPy; card embeddings as vectors; similarity.

lessons.title: Calculus you actually need: slopes and gradients
lessons.summary: Derivatives as slopes, partial derivatives, the gradient, the chain rule (intuition), gradient descent on a 1-D and 2-D function.

lessons.title: Your first models from scratch: linear and logistic regression
lessons.summary: Predict a number, predict a probability (P(win) from elixir and tower HP), sigmoid, log-loss, training with NumPy only.

lessons.title: Measuring classifiers: accuracy, NLL, calibration, AUC
lessons.summary: Top-1 accuracy (card 65.3%), negative log-likelihood, softmax over many classes, calibration error, ROC and AUC (the C-live test).

lessons.title: Overfitting, splits and choosing the best checkpoint
lessons.summary: Train / validation / test, held-out data, early stopping, regularisation, why the project keeps sealed blocks it reads last.

lessons.title: Neural networks and backpropagation
lessons.summary: Neurons, layers, activations, an MLP, the forward pass, backpropagation by hand on a tiny network, then in NumPy.

lessons.title: PyTorch: tensors, autograd and the training loop
lessons.summary: Tensors, devices (CPU / CUDA), autograd, nn.Module, optimisers (Adam), DataLoader, saving and loading .pt checkpoints and checking their sha.

lessons.title: Embeddings, attention and transformers
lessons.summary: Embedding tables for cards, attention as weighted lookup, a transformer encoder layer, how the bot's model reads the board and its memory features.

lessons.title: Many heads, sampling and temperature
lessons.summary: One network with card / cell / timing / ability outputs, softmax sampling, temperature (T 1 vs 0.5 vs greedy), masks for unaffordable cards.

lessons.title: Model size and scaling curves
lessons.summary: Parameters vs held-out loss, noise between seeds, reading the project's 2.5M-20.8M curve, when bigger stops helping.

lessons.title: Making training fast: GPUs, memory and batch size
lessons.summary: Batches and minibatches, GPU memory and out-of-memory errors (arm D's u3 crash), micro-batching, TF32 / precision, CUDA graphs, torch.compile, determinism vs speed.

lessons.title: PROJECT 6: Predict the next card
lessons.summary: Train a small PyTorch model that predicts an opponent's next card from the previous cards they played (a toy version of the opponent model), report accuracy and NLL on held-out data, and compare model sizes.

parts.title: Part G - Imitation learning: learning from humans

lessons.title: Behaviour cloning from replays
lessons.summary: Turning human replays into (state, action) rows, the HF and pro datasets, training a policy to copy people.

lessons.title: Fine-tuning and distribution shift
lessons.summary: Why a model trained on one population plays differently against another, fine-tuning on live opponents (ftR), held-out live splits.

lessons.title: Per-decision vs closed-loop evaluation
lessons.summary: Level A (one decision at a time) vs level B (whole games), compounding errors, why a well-calibrated opponent still lets X-Bows lock.

lessons.title: Measuring human-likeness
lessons.summary: Style statistics, standardised differences and RMS, a classifier that tries to tell bot from human (C-AUC), the human noise floor.

lessons.title: RL basics: agent, environment, reward, return
lessons.summary: States, actions, rewards, episodes, discounted return, exploration; a toy elixir game you can play by hand.

lessons.title: Value, advantage and baselines
lessons.summary: Value functions, Monte Carlo vs temporal difference, the advantage, GAE, leave-one-out baselines (match_loo).

lessons.title: Policy gradients
lessons.summary: REINFORCE derived step by step, why it is noisy, variance reduction, implementing it on the toy game.

lessons.title: PPO: the algorithm the project trains with
lessons.summary: Probability ratios, clipping, KL divergence and the 0.02 KL stop, entropy, epochs and minibatches, decoupled PPO for stale data.

lessons.title: Reward design and reward hacking
lessons.summary: Sparse win rewards, potential-based shaping (Phi = P(win) - 0.5), simulator exploits, why the project bans hand-coded habit rules.

lessons.title: Self-play, leagues and opponents
lessons.summary: Training against copies and pools, exploiters, why opponent quality limits what the bot learns, the calibration arms and their plateau.

lessons.title: Counterfactual credit: forking the simulator
lessons.summary: What-if rollouts from the same state, common random numbers, why the SIM prices the Rocket negative, auditing a training signal.

lessons.title: Staying close to a reference: KL pulls and drift
lessons.summary: KL anchors (beta, th_anchor), frozen heads, drift monitors, and the owner's 'no leash on our own model' rule.

lessons.title: Distributed training: actors, learners and throughput
lessons.summary: Producers and learner, the fast loop, overlap, matches per hour vs learning per update, the critical batch size.

lessons.title: From SIM to live: gates, trials and promotion
lessons.summary: Pooled SIM gates with confidence intervals, the 30-match safety trial with auto-revert, the 150-match block, observing after promotion.

lessons.title: PROJECT 7: Train a PPO agent on your mini simulator
lessons.summary: Turn Project 4's simulator into an environment, write PPO in PyTorch, train an agent that beats a scripted opponent, and evaluate it with a confidence interval.

parts.title: Part I - How ML research is done (in this project)

lessons.title: Reproducibility: seeds, hashes and pinned versions
lessons.summary: Config hashes, checkpoint shas, pinned engine builds, 'absent key = byte-identical', why runs on different builds are never compared.

lessons.title: Keeping a research log: ledgers, STATUS files and restart points
lessons.summary: Writing down what ran and what it showed so anyone can resume; checkpoint naming and registries.

lessons.title: Thinking like a researcher: measured, plausible, contradicted
lessons.summary: Hypotheses vs findings, grading every claim, testing a diagnosis before acting on it, iterating instead of discarding.

lessons.title: Working with AI coding agents
lessons.summary: Writing a clear brief, checking an agent's numbers yourself, why workers re-tally Codex results, common failure modes.

lessons.title: Secrets, safety and rules of the game
lessons.summary: API keys and why the exposed key must be revoked, .gitignore, never committing secrets, game terms of service and live-play risk.

lessons.title: CAPSTONE: Reproduce and explain one real experiment
lessons.summary: Pick one experiment from the ledger (e.g. the opponent calibration arms), explain its design, recompute its numbers from the raw logs with your own code, and write a short report a teammate could act on.
